Alex: Quick signal — saw a throughput regression on mistral-8x MQA runs after the recent kernel-picker change. Seq=1024 steady-state throughput down ~18%, paged-KV evict rate up 2.4x. RoPE scaling flip seems correlated.
Maria: ugh, can you paste the benchmark flags + a short perf snippet?
Alex: bench command I used: `./tools/bench_throughput --model mistral-8x --kv-mode=mqa --rope-scale=1.15 --kernel-policy=auto --batch-target=64 --seq-len=1024`
Alex: pprof-like sample (hot lines):
```
matmul_generic            42.7%  42.7% kernel
kv_page_copy             18.9%  61.6% runtime
kv_gather_align         10.2%  71.8% kernel
matmul_fused             6.4%  78.2% kernel (previously dominant)
other                    21.8%       
```
Alex: note kernel switch: before the picker picked `matmul_fused` heavily; after change it favors `matmul_generic` for some head/layout combos.
Jia: do we have num_key_value_heads + kv_dim for the load? (those often flip kernel selection)
Alex: config: `num_key_value_heads=32`, `kv_dim=64` (per head), so total kv width=2048.
Jia: that 32 head count + rope-scale >1 is suspicious: RoPE scaling changes effective token-lambda which shifts matmul shapes (heads x dim) and the kernel heuristics rely on those dims. Also paged-KV fragmentation > more small copies -> matmul_generic wins.
Sam: Could be batching heuristic too — if the batcher is coalescing more small requests into big token blocks, we might hit different kernel thresholds. Are you running token-target batching or latency-target?
Alex: token-target=64. I saw larger coalesced batches in the trace during the regression period.
Maria: quick experiments to run (short):
- force kernel hint to fused: `export REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=matmul_fused; ./tools/bench_throughput ...`
- lower num_kv_heads to 16 to see kernel pick and throughput
- try kv layout `packed` vs `interleaved` (`--kv-layout=packed`)
- run `--batch-mode=latency` to see if batching reduces fragmentation
Jia: also try aligning kv_dim to 128 multiples (64->128) to see if GPU matmul tiling picks different kernels. Small change, big kernel selector effect.
perf-bot: Auto-report: https://perf.internal/graphs/2107777777 (shows 18% throughput drop, 2.4x KV page faults, kernel distribution shift). :chart_with_upwards_trend: :exclamation:
Alex: ran forced-fused hint: throughput recovered ~12% but not fully; still ~6% below baseline. So fused helps but doesn't fully explain increased KV copy overhead.
Sam: hypothesis: RoPE scaling increases effective sequence-key variance -> KV pages more frequently considered cold -> more paging/gather ops -> copy overhead + matmul_generic win.
Maria: plan: bisect the kernel-picker change (PRs last week) + run the three micro-experiments Jia listed. If bisect points to selector logic, revert heuristics. If not, try kv-layout fallback in runtime: prefer `packed` for high-head counts.
Alex: quick commands for the team to run locally:
```bash
# baseline run (auto-select)
./tools/bench_throughput --model mistral-8x --kv-mode=mqa --rope-scale=1.15 --seq-len=1024 --batch-target=64
# force fused hint
REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=matmul_fused ./tools/bench_throughput --model mistral-8x --kv-mode=mqa --rope-scale=1.15 --seq-len=1024 --batch-target=64
# try fewer kv heads
./tools/bench_throughput --model mistral-8x --kv-mode=mqa --num-kv-heads=16 --kv-dim=128 --seq-len=1024
```
Jia: I'll spin up a rig and run the head/dim/kv-layout matrix overnight and post results.
Sam: I'll look at the batcher traces and see if token-target coalescing behavior changed after the batching heuristics tweak.
Maria: If we confirm fragmentation + kernel pick interplay, we should add a small runtime guard: when `num_kv_heads >= 24 && rope_scale > 1.1` prefer `packed` layout and bias kernel selection to fused-like kernels. Add a telemetry counter for `forced_kernel_hint` + `kv_page_faults` to Console.
Alex: assigning follow-ups: Jia (head/dim matrix), Sam (batcher trace), Maria (bisect + telemetry). I'll collect numbers and open an incident-style thread if we need a hotfix.
perf-bot: Noted. Test-run checklist created: https://perf.internal/checklists/2107777777
Alex: thanks — will post results ASAP. :thumbsup:
